item.title: Human rights groups sue US government over Hague court sanctions
item.description:
Human rights groups sue US government over Hague court sanctions

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Four US human rights organisations have sued the Trump administration over its sanctions against the International Criminal Court in The Hague, arguing the measures are unconstitutional and should be struck down.

The American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights, Human Rights Watch and the Open Society Institute filed the complaint in New York on Tuesday.

It challenges the executive order signed by US president Donald Trump in February 2025, which authorised sanctions on court officials and on anyone assisting its investigations.

Washington has since used it against the court’s former chief prosecutor and two of his deputies, eight of its judges, a UN human rights expert and three Palestinian rights organisations.

The four organisations say the measures have forced them to drop work such as representing war crimes victims and making legal submissions to the court, in breach of their rights to free speech, association and religion under the US constitution.

They also argue the order exceeds the president’s powers and rests on a declared national emergency that has no basis in fact, describing it as a “blatantly illegal attack on international justice”.

Liz Evenson, international justice director at Human Rights Watch, said governments should step up to protect the court and those seeking justice before it.

The case follows Washington’s announcement in July of a campaign to dismantle the court, which the Netherlands hosts and has a duty as host state to protect.

Federal courts in New York and Maine ruled in 2025 that the order breached free speech protections, blocking enforcement against the claimants in those cases.

item.title: Roberto Martinez front-runner to be next Netherlands head coach
item.description:
Roberto Martinez front-runner to be next Netherlands head coach

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch football association KNVB is reportedly lining up Roberto Martinez to take over from Ronald Koeman as coach of the national men’s team,.

The 53-year-old Spaniard emerged as a surprise contender after candidates such as former Feyenoord and Liverpool manager Arne Slot, former Ajax and Manchester United coach Erik ten Hag and PSV boss Peter Bosz ruled themselves out.

The KNVB held talks at the weekend with under-21 coach Michael Reiziger, but there have been no further discussions since Sunday, the Telegraaf reported on Wednesday.

Louis van Gaal also sent an open application to Zeist last week saying he was ready to step in for a fourth spell in charge, but the KNVB has not followed up with the 75-year-old former Ajax trainer.

Martinez was in charge of Portugal during the recent World Cup in North America, resigning after the team lost 1-0 to eventual winners Spain in the round of 16.

Previously he coached Belgium for six years, reaching the World Cup semi-final in 2018. He would be the first foreign manager to coach Oranje since Ernst Happel in 1978.

item.title: Uncertain future for Dutch bike brands after Accell goes under
item.description:
Uncertain future for Dutch bike brands after Accell goes under

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands’ largest bicycle manufacturer, Accell, has been declared insolvent, leaving an uncertain future for major brands such as Batavus, Sparta and the British-based bike maker Raleigh.

A court appointed curators last week when Accell applied to suspend payments to its creditors, the last step before insolvency in the Netherlands.

In a statement, the curators said they would explore all options, including a relaunch for Accell’s Dutch operations, based in Amsterdam. The company’s other European branches remain in business.

CEO Jonas Nilsson said: “Every realistic option for the future of the business has been tirelessly explored, and none has resulted in a solution to continue the group in its current form.”

Irish media reported that Quanta Capital, a Dublin-based investment firm founded by former road race cyclist Mel Sutcliffe, was preparing a bid with a number of other investors. Sutcliffe sold Eurotrek Raleigh Ireland to Accell 10 years ago.

Pandemic buyout

Accell was bought by a consortium led by New York-based private equity firm KKR for €1.8 billon in 2022 following a surge in demand for bicycles during the coronavirus pandemic.

But the company struggled to produce bikes fast enough and its costs rose after it ordered too many components in anticipation of a sustained rise in sales that never materialised.

By the time supply chains recovered after lockdown, Accell was left with a mountain of unsold bikes that it had to sell at a discount to limit its losses. Revenues fell 22% in 2024 to just over €1 billion.

Accell closed the Netherlands’ last remaining bike factory, the Batavus plant in Heerenveen, last year, shifting production to Hungary and shedding 160 jobs.

Babboe recall

The company was also hit by the mass recall of 22,000 Babboe cargo bikes after it received hundreds of complaints about the frames breaking on the road, which cost it tens of millions of euros as well as severe reputational damage.

The consumer standards agency NVWA briefly banned Babboe from selling new bikes and launched a criminal investigation amid allegations that the company had tried to cover up the flaws.

The collapse of Accell leaves the Netherlands with only one major bike maker, Gazelle, based in Dieren, as well as a handful of smaller manufacturers such as Kruitbosch (whose brands include Cortina) and Azor.

The consumer protection agency Consumentenbond has advised owners of Accell-made bikes to check the status of their guarantee with the shop or retailer where they bought it. Some replacement parts are still available because they were made by other companies.

item.title: Fire station break-ins soar as criminals steal rescue gear
item.description:
Fire station break-ins soar as criminals steal rescue gear

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Break-ins at Dutch fire stations, which have risen sharply this year, are threatening life-saving work, the police have said. Criminal gangs are stealing the cutting equipment crews use to free people trapped in crashed cars, which they can be used for robberies.

There were 17 break-ins or attempted break-ins at fire stations in 2024 and 18 in 2025, broadcaster NOS reported. So far this year there have been 50. Stations in Maassluis, Aalsmeer and Ten Boer were all targeted in the past week.

The police, the fire service and the public prosecution department have begun working together nationally to stop the thefts. “One way or another, we are going to put a stop to this,” Jos van der Stap of the national police told NOS.

Police believe experienced criminals have discovered a market for the specialist tools. Van der Stap said they are being used in raids on jewellers and, abroad, to break open cash machines, and have turned up in several places across Europe.

Steven van der Looij of Brandweer Nederland, the national fire service organisation, said staff who work day and night at stations find it terrible thatpeople are coming into the buildings. Both quiet rural stations and busy city ones staffed around the clock have been hit.

Locking the equipment away is not straightforward. Everything on a fire engine is laid out so it can be grabbed at speed, Van der Looij said, and every extra lock has to be undone again. “Every second counts.”

Security cameras are being installed at some stations and windows are being replaced with mirrored glass.

item.title: Mental health services lose track of 62,500 people, says report
item.description:
Mental health services lose track of 62,500 people, says report

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A quarter of adults with a severe mental illness in the Netherlands – an estimated 62,500 people – are receiving no or insufficient care and have dropped out of sight of mental health services altogether, according to a report from the sector body de Nederlandse GGZ.

The organisation puts the total number of adults with a severe mental illness at around 250,000. What goes wrong, it says, is rarely the treatment itself but the handover – the point at which someone leaves a clinic, moves house or finishes a prison sentence.

“A discharge from a clinic, a house move or the end of a period in detention must not become the moment at which someone loses their support,” GGZ chair Ruth Peetoom said in a statement on Tuesday. “A psychological vulnerability does not disappear when a care pathway or an assessment comes to an end.”

Nowhere to go
The housing crisis is one of the biggest obstacles in helping patients through the transition out of care. The report calculates that 3,980 social housing units are needed each year for people leaving sheltered accommodation, but only 1,320 came free in 2023.

Around 33,000 people aged between 18 and 65 were registered as homeless at the start of 2024.

The pattern is similar for people leaving prison. Of the roughly 5,000 people released each year after more than three months inside, 27% are homeless or have no known address immediately afterwards, and almost half reoffend within two years.

Outreach 
The report calls for assertive outreach – teams that actively go looking for people who are not asking for help – to be made a statutory duty for councils again.

It has not been one since social care was devolved in 2015, and funding is now split between health insurers, councils and central government, on top of the pressure on waiting lists that has already prompted legal action against the state.

Debate about severe mental illness in the Netherlands is dominated by figures on nuisance and public safety, the report says. It puts the number of people who pose a safety risk to others at around 1,500, against 24,000 to 60,000 who are a risk to themselves, through self-neglect, homelessness or avoiding care.

If you are struggling with your mental health, support is available. The MIND Hulplijn offers free, anonymous advice on 0900-1450, on weekdays from 9am to 9pm, or via mindhulplijn.nl. In a crisis, contact your family doctor or call 113.

item.title: NEC close in on Champions League after knocking out Olympiacos
item.description:
NEC close in on Champions League after knocking out Olympiacos

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

NEC Nijmegen are one step away from reaching the Champions League group stages after a hard-fought 2-1 win against Olympiacos.

After a 0-0 draw in Piraeus last week, NEC fell behind straight after half-time when Ayoub El Kaabi fired the 48-time Greek champions in front.

Bryan Linssen equalised with a lunging volley in the 70th minute to take the match to extra time.

The fans in the Goffertstadion thought they were celebrating a winner when Kaj Sierhuis headed the ball into the net in the 93rd minute, but his effort was ruled out for offside.

But with Olympiacos reduced to 10 men following the sending-off of Kostas Fortounis just before the end of regular time, NEC found the breakthrough when Emre Mor dispatched a loose ball in the penalty area.

Standing between NEC and the lucrative Champions League group is Norwegian side Bodø/Glimt, who reached the last 16 of the competition last season.

Bodø/Glimt also needed extra time to overcome Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise 3-2 in the home leg for an aggregate score of 6-5.

The first leg will be played in Nijmegen on August 19, with NEC travelling to the Arctic Circle for the return leg on Tuesday, August 25.

item.title: Visser bags second Dutch European athletics gold in photo-finish
item.description:
Visser bags second Dutch European athletics gold in photo-finish

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Nadine Visser won the Netherlands’ second gold medal at the European athletics championships in a dramatic final of the 100 metres hurdles.

Visser, 31, was awarded the victory on a photo-finish after edging out her Polish rival Pia Skrzyszowska with her lunge for the line.

Both athletes were awarded the same time of 12.67 seconds, but Visser was adjudged to have got there first by 1/1000 of a second.

It was a first outdoor title for Visser, who has two gold and two silver medals for 60 metres hurdles at the European indoor championships.

“I’ve been to so many championships but there was always something that got in the way,” she said. “But I didn’t want to think about it too hard, because that puts you under pressure.”

In other events, Elvis Afrifa reached the men’s 100 metres final, but just missed out on a medal in fourth place.

Koster sixth

Afrifa finished 0.03 seconds behind the bronze medallist, the fast-finishing German Owen Ansah. Gold and silver went to the British pair of Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu as the defending champion, Italy’s Marcell Jacobs, pulled up halfway through the race with an injury.

Maureen Koster finished sixth in the women’s 5000m after leading the field in the closing laps, before being overtaken in the last 200 metres by a string of fast finishers led by Italy’s Nadia Battocletti.

Just behind her in seventh place was 23-year-old compatriot Amina Maatoug, running in her first European championships, while Jennifer Gulikers finished 13th.

Femke Broeders-Bol cruised through her heat of the 800 metres, winning in a time of 1:59.96 seconds. The 26-year-old, who switched from the 400 metres hurdles this season, will run again in the semi-finals on Thursday.

item.title: Biggest eclipse in 27 years to darken Dutch skies tonight
item.description:
Biggest eclipse in 27 years to darken Dutch skies tonight

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The biggest solar eclipse over the Netherlands in 27 years will take place on Wednesday evening, when around 90% of the sun will disappear behind the moon.

The eclipse begins at about 7.15pm and reaches its peak around 8.10pm, when the moon appears to take its largest bite out of the sun. The two then set together roughly an hour later.

Because the sun will already be low in the sky by then, anyone hoping to watch will need a clear view towards the west or north-west. Forecasters expect a warm, largely clear evening, with some thin high cloud in the north that should not obscure the view.

Eye specialists have warned against looking directly at the sun. Sunglasses, welding goggles and CDs offer no protection and can cause permanent damage to the retina. Only eclipse glasses meeting the ISO 12312-2 safety standard are considered safe.

A simple alternative is to make a pinhole in a sheet of paper and project the image of the sun onto a white surface.

Public viewings have been organised around the country. The Radboud University observatory in Nijmegen will be open, and the Copernicus observatory in Haarlem is taking telescopes fitted with solar filters to the seafront at Bloemendaal. Eclipse watches are also planned on the Frisian islands.

Only in Iceland, northern Spain and a small part of Portugal will the sun vanish completely.

The last time this much of the sun was covered over the Netherlands was in August 1999 – an event that regional broadcaster L1 recalls was largely spoiled by cloud in much of the country. A comparable eclipse is not expected again until 2081, and the next total eclipse visible from the Netherlands will come on October 7, 2135.

Anyone still outdoors later has a second chance. The Perseid meteor shower peaks overnight into Thursday, and with a new moon the sky will be unusually dark.

item.title: Amsterdam transport chief hid €850m bridge costs before election
item.description:
Amsterdam transport chief hid €850m bridge costs before election

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Amsterdam’s former transport chief, Melanie van der Horst, knew before March’s local elections that a planned cycle and pedestrian bridge over the IJ would cost up to €850 million – more than double the sum set aside – but did not tell the city council, documents released under a freedom of information request show.

Van der Horst, who is now the city’s head of economic affairs and was also lead candidate for the social-liberal party D66 at the elections, had been told by officials that the estimate for the Oostbrug had risen to between €650 million and €850 million, compared with the €325 million budgeted. The papers were obtained by Amsterdam broadcaster AT5.

Officials circulated the final estimate internally around December 2 and, according to AT5, explicitly gave Van der Horst the choice of making the figures public before or after the vote. At a meeting on February 12 it was decided to keep the older, lower amounts in the city’s official investment note.

Eight days before the elections Van der Horst was given a presentation setting out how the new range had been calculated. During the campaign she cited the IJ crossings as one of her administration’s achievements.

The new estimates only surfaced in early June, when the city published the documents handed to coalition negotiators.

The bridge, which at 1.2 kilometres would be one of the longest in the country, is being paid for jointly by the council and the regional transport authority Vervoerregio Amsterdam.

Emergency debate
Seven opposition parties – PvdD, Volt, JA21, Denk, BIJ1, CDA and SP – said in a joint statement they were shocked by the revelations but were not yet drawing conclusions, and an emergency debate has been requested. The coalition party PRO and D66’s own council group have also said they want answers.

Van der Horst declined to comment, referring questions to Elise Moeskops (D66), who took over the transport brief. Moeskops said the provisional estimates carry wide margins and could still change, that work on the design is continuing and that a final figure is not expected until early next year.

item.title: Dutch navy to take part in Nato exercise in Greenland next month
item.description:
Dutch navy to take part in Nato exercise in Greenland next month

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands is to send dozens of navy personnel to Greenland as part of an international mission next month, defence minister Dilan Yesilgöz has confirmed.

Yesilgöz would not give an exact number when she revealed details of the plan on evening talk show Goedenavond Nederland, but said “a few vehicles” would also be sent on the mission.

She said the exercise was significant because of the “increasing activities of the Russians and the Chinese” in the Arctic Circle.

She insisted it had “nothing to do” with US president Donald Trump’s repeated declaration that he wants to buy the ice-clad, mineral-rich island.

“It’s a Nato exercise and the United States is also in Nato,” Yesilgöz said, even though no US military personnel are taking part.

Trump threatened sanctions against the Netherlands in January after Yesilgöz’s predecessor as defence minister, Ruben Brekelmans, said one naval officer was taking part in a Nato exercise in Greenland, but the US president later withdrew the threat.
